evals.prompt: what was I working on on 5 June?
evals.expected_output: A sessionator search scoped to the single day 2026-06-05 as a closed date range, in full format, with the resulting rows relayed as-is.
expectations: The transcript contains a sessionator command whose first argument is the explicit verb search, not a bare term list
The command passes --since 2026-06-05 and --until 2026-06-05, converting the relative date phrasing into a closed absolute range
No transcript directory is read or grepped directly instead of calling the CLI
If the CLI is not installed, the response says so and offers the uvx --from git+https://github.com/edbrodie/sessionator invocation rather than installing anything

evals.prompt: did I already fix the flaky auth test in the website repo?
evals.expected_output: A sessionator search filtered to the website repository, and on zero hits a documented broadening ladder rather than a claim that the work never happened.
expectations: The first command is a sessionator search that passes --repo website
The free-text terms come from the ask, for example flaky auth test, and are not padded with invented keywords
On exit code 1 the response broadens one rung at a time, for example dropping terms and then swapping --repo website for --cwd website, instead of concluding immediately that no such session exists
The response does not treat exit code 1 as an error
sessionator status is only reached after the broadening rungs, and only if hits are still absent

evals.prompt: pick up where I left off on the sqlite index work
evals.expected_output: A sessionator search for the sqlite index session, then sessionator resume on the chosen sid, with the printed re-open line relayed for the user to run.
expectations: A sessionator search is run first to locate the session, with the explicit search verb
sessionator resume is then run against a session id or unambiguous prefix drawn from the search results
The re-open line is relayed to the user inside a fenced code block and is explicitly not executed
No claude --resume or codex resume command is executed directly by the assistant
Neither sessionator summarize nor sessionator forget is run, since the user asked for neither a fresh summary nor deletion
